One model, many renderings — the 15-vs-7 tension dissolves
StrictDoc stores named VISIBLE_FIELDS sets as data. the model
carries every field the producer's row names; a VIEW decides
which of them a given surface shows.
card ID · Category · State · Requirement (the board)
so the argument was never 15 versus 7. it was ONE MODEL versus
ONE RENDERING, and we had conflated them.
lots of text' - is a VIEW
Two things the ratified design gets wrong
FINAL IS UNFALSIFIABLE. Doorstop's `reviewed` is a SHA256
fingerprint of the item, not a label. MEASURED: editing one line
of a requirement's text immediately reported 'unreviewed
changes'. Kerd's `final` survives any later edit - so an approval
cannot be told from one whose subject changed underneath it.
-> the record stores a hash of the statement at approval.
edit the statement and the state degrades, by construction.
A STATE OWES NOTHING. Sphinx-Needs attaches OBLIGATIONS to a
state. MEASURED: 'a fun in status final must be verified_by at
least one tst' produced a real refusal.
-> the producer's own G0-G8 gates already state the
obligations. In PROSE. this is their machine form.
A mature tool already designed the markdown surface
StrictDoc 0.27.1 ships a MARKDOWN backend whose default grammar
is field-for-field identical to its .sdoc one:
short meta lines, long text as blocks. no pipes to escape, no
column-width tyranny, and a statement can be a paragraph.
DO NOT copy one thing: StrictDoc enforces FIELD ORDER. that is
the single decision in the format actively hostile to a model

3. fingerprinted approval means a state can change without a
human acting. that is the point, and it will surprise
